name: San Pedro Town
tagline: Three sand streets and every golf cart on the island
description: The centre of Ambergris Caye, three parallel streets running along the beach with the shops, restaurants, dive operators and the water taxi dock. It is walkable end to end and is where almost everything on the island happens.
bestFor: Anyone who wants everything within walking distance
pros: Water taxis to Caye Caulker and the mainland
The widest choice of restaurants and dive shops
cons: Golf cart traffic on narrow streets
Busy and noisy in high season

name: South of Town
tagline: The condo strip towards the airstrip
description: The coast running south from town past the airstrip, a stretch of condominium developments, small resorts and restaurants with a quieter beach and easier parking. It is where much of the long-stay foreign population lives.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a condo and a calmer beach
pros: Quieter than town with better beaches
Most of the long-stay rental stock
Five minutes to town by golf cart

name: North Ambergris
tagline: Over the bridge, and getting more expensive
description: The island north of the Boca del Rio bridge, developed steadily over the last two decades with resorts, condominiums and restaurants along a road that gets rougher the further you go. The beach improves and the prices rise with the distance.
bestFor: Anyone wanting the best beach and willing to drive for it
pros: The best beaches on the caye
cons: The most expensive part of the island
Bridge toll and a rough road north
Isolated from town for anything spontaneous

name: Caye Caulker
tagline: The smaller, slower, cheaper island next door
description: A separate caye forty-five minutes south by water taxi, smaller than Ambergris, with sand streets, no cars at all and a motto of go slow that it takes seriously. It is what San Pedro was thirty years ago and costs a fraction as much.
bestFor: Budget stays wanting the reef without San Pedro's prices
pros: No cars at all, only bicycles and carts
The Split for swimming and the same reef offshore
cons: A separate island, not a neighbourhood
Very small, exhausted in a week
